note: The Swift test file hardcodes no ciphertext: every test there is a round-trip or an error case. The key/nonce/plaintext/aad inputs below are transcribed from it verbatim; the ciphertext and tag are derived (see each vector's derivation). One published vector from the XChaCha draft is included so a broken port fails against the standard, not only against us.

seal.name: draft_xchacha_a_3_1
seal.derivation: Transcribed from the draft, then reproduced byte for byte by the script that emitted this file.
seal.note: The unambiguous one: if this fails, the port is not XChaCha20-Poly1305 at all.

seal.name: bitchat_seal_and_open_roundtrip
seal.derivation: Computed with a pure-python XChaCha20-Poly1305 written from RFC 8439 plus draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha-03 and validated, before use, against RFC 8439 section 2.8.2 and draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha-03 sections 2.2.1 and A.3.1. Construction transcribed from bitchat/Nostr/XChaCha20Poly1305Compat.swift: subkey = HChaCha20(key, nonce24[0..16]), nonce12 = 00000000 || nonce24[16..24], then IETF ChaCha20-Poly1305.
seal.note: Their round-trip test, pinned to concrete output bytes.

seal.name: bitchat_seal_and_open_with_aad
seal.derivation: Computed with a pure-python XChaCha20-Poly1305 written from RFC 8439 plus draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha-03 and validated, before use, against RFC 8439 section 2.8.2 and draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha-03 sections 2.2.1 and A.3.1. Construction transcribed from bitchat/Nostr/XChaCha20Poly1305Compat.swift: subkey = HChaCha20(key, nonce24[0..16]), nonce12 = 00000000 || nonce24[16..24], then IETF ChaCha20-Poly1305.
seal.note: AAD is authenticated, not encrypted: ciphertext length equals plaintext length. bitchat's DM path always passes an empty AAD, so this vector exists to prove the AAD is wired to the MAC and not silently dropped.

seal.note: Pairs with bitchat_same_plaintext_nonce_02; the two ciphertexts must differ.

seal.note: 256 bytes spans four ChaCha20 blocks and a multi-block Poly1305 accumulation.
